records.limitations: Derived display measurement, not a hazard or trafficability product: slope = atan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2)) computed by team/jezero/terrain/build_slope.mjs on the display pixel grid from bilinearly sampled DTM elevations, with Mars ground spacing (r = 3,396,190 m). records.coverage: Slope in degrees over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E, from a 201 x 205 elevation grid (0.01 degree, about 0.59 km) sampled from the Mars Trek elevation-profile service (MGS MOLA, Global DEM). 26 display tiles, zooms 5-9. Grid: /maps/oxia/elevation-grid.json.
records.limitations: Regional slope from MOLA (~463 m). Small banks, boulders and walking-scale hazards are not resolved. Not a safety assessment. MOLA only across the whole area: the sharper HRSC-derived detail seen in parts of the hillshade is not in this layer. Tiles end at zoom 9; closer zooms enlarge them. Slope from central differences on a 0.01 degree grid interpolated from MOLA, using Mars 2000 sphere distances (R = 3,396,190 m); steep short slopes are smoothed out, so real local slopes can exceed the mapped class. The >20 degree class marks slopes beyond NASA's 20 degree suited-walking figure: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B, Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations (Oct 19, 2020), p.38, 'Walking up/down/across a slope of up to 20°' (source oxia-nasa-eva-exp-0042); NASA ICES-2025-129 (Kim et al., funded by the NASA Mars Campaign Office), p.7, treats slopes beyond +/-20 degrees as inaccessible no-go zones (source oxia-nasa-ices-2025-129). That figure is lunar-derived and Mars gravity is higher. In this area 56 of 41,205 cells (18.8 km2, 0.14%) exceed 20 degrees, mostly one patch near 17.21 N, 335.07 E.

records.coverage: Mars Trek THEMIS night-IR global mosaic over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E: 75 derived display tiles, Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-10 (source level 9, about 81 m per pixel), coloured with an inferno display ramp. No gaps in this area.
records.limitations: Relative brightness only: the 8-bit mosaic values are not calibrated temperatures and are not thermal-inertia values. Observation period not stated by Mars Trek (the 'oct2018' in the layer name refers to the 2018 mosaic release). Night-time brightness mainly reflects thermal inertia (brighter = holds heat, e.g. rock or indurated surfaces; darker = loose sand or dust), but it can also vary with season, local time and dust. Mosaic of many orbits with stretched brightness between images, so strip-to-strip seams can appear. Colours are a display ramp (matplotlib 'inferno') applied to the uncalibrated 8-bit values; they do not mark temperature or thermal-inertia thresholds. Display-grade, nearest-neighbour resampled; not terrain-safety evidence.
records.attribution: NASA Mars Odyssey THEMIS · night-IR global mosaic (2018 release) · via NASA JPL Mars Trek

items.label: Yellow: brightest, holds heat at night (likely rock or firm ground)
